## Risk flags (triggered, most-severe first)
### R05 · NOI quality / manufactured NOI  —  **CRITICAL** (L2)
- **Category:** NOI Quality
- **Evidence:** Seller Year-1 NOI ($6,911,304) exceeds T-12 actual ($6,859,742) via expense cuts, not revenue: Turnover -32.1% and R&M -25.7% below T-12.
- **OM page:** null
- **Why it matters:** NOI lifted by cutting expenses below trailing actuals — rather than growing revenue — is not durable. It is the single most common OM overstatement and directly inflates value at the going-in cap.
- **Estimated financial impact:** ~$67,527/yr of NOI overstated → ≈$1,286,229 of value at 5.3%.
- **Recommended next action:** Re-underwrite controllable expenses to T-12 actuals; treat 'market adjustments' as unproven until third-party bids support them.
- **Additional DD required:** Yes

### R01 · Occupancy & leased-rate integrity  —  **CRITICAL** (L2)
- **Category:** Occupancy & Vacancy
- **Evidence:** 96.0% occupied but only 85.0% leased — a 11-pt gap (~24 units under notice) vs an underwritten 5.0% vacancy.
- **OM page:** null
- **Why it matters:** Physical occupancy counts bodies in units; leased rate counts signed leases net of notices. A large leased-below-occupied gap signals a forward vacancy wave that the seller's underwritten vacancy does not capture.
- **Estimated financial impact:** ~$782,059/yr NOI exposure if leased rate holds (≈$14,896,370 of value at 5.3%).
- **Recommended next action:** Pull the notice-to-vacate report and 60-day leasing velocity; re-underwrite vacancy to the leased rate until velocity proves otherwise.
- **Additional DD required:** Yes

### R08 · Capital-expenditure & reserve adequacy  —  **CRITICAL** (L2)
- **Category:** Capital / Value-Add
- **Evidence:** Reserves only $137/unit for a 2015 12-story asset; the marketed value-add thesis carries $0 of renovation capital.
- **OM page:** null
- **Why it matters:** Thin reserves plus a value-add thesis with zero renovation capital means the upside is claimed but unfunded — the buyer pays for NOI growth that requires unbudgeted capital to achieve.
- **Estimated financial impact:** Reserve shortfall ~$24,634/yr (≈$469,219 of value); interior renovation est. $1.5–2.5M unfunded.
- **Recommended next action:** Budget interior + fitness-center capital and raise reserves to ≥$250/unit for a 12-story asset; net the capital from the bid.
- **Additional DD required:** Yes

### R20 · Missing due-diligence coverage  —  **HIGH** (L1) · guardrail
- **Category:** Due Diligence
- **Evidence:** 8 critical DD items not provided in the OM: Full unit-level rent roll, T-12 operating statement + GL, Leased-vs-occupied / NTV report, Bound insurance policy + loss runs, …
- **OM page:** null
- **Why it matters:** Core underwriting inputs absent from the OM mean the screening rests on marketing figures; the deal cannot clear IC until they are obtained.
- **Estimated financial impact:** Screening rests on marketing figures until DD is received.
- **Recommended next action:** Issue the DD request list; do not advance to IC until the rent roll, T-12 statement, leases, and PCA are received.
- **Additional DD required:** Yes

### R03 · Year-1 rent-growth aggressiveness  —  **HIGH** (L2)
- **Category:** Revenue / Rent
- **Evidence:** Seller underwrites +3.5% Year-1 rent growth off the T-3, yet T-12 GSR ($7,601,310) exceeds T-3 annualized ($7,556,129) — rents are decelerating, not accelerating.
- **OM page:** null
- **Why it matters:** Front-loaded rent growth inflates Year-1 NOI and therefore going-in value. It is only credible with signed-lease trade-out evidence, especially when trailing rents are flat-to-down.
- **Estimated financial impact:** ~$264,465 of Year-1 revenue not yet in place.
- **Recommended next action:** Require signed new-lease and renewal trade-out data for the last 6 months before crediting Year-1 growth.
- **Additional DD required:** Yes

### R06 · Expense anomaly — insurance step-change  —  **MEDIUM** (L1)
- **Category:** Expenses
- **Evidence:** Insurance underwritten at $139,431 vs T-12 $57,596 — a 142.1% step-change.
- **OM page:** null
- **Why it matters:** A >50% swing between trailing and underwritten insurance means either T-12 is understated (further NOI drag) or the UW is padded — either way the true run-rate is unknown without the bound policy.
- **Estimated financial impact:** $81,835 of unexplained annual expense swing.
- **Recommended next action:** Obtain the bound policy and 5-year loss runs; set insurance to the quoted renewal, not a $/unit rule of thumb.
- **Additional DD required:** Yes

### R09 · Deferred maintenance & building systems  —  **MEDIUM** (L1)
- **Category:** Physical / Capital
- **Evidence:** No PCA in the OM. Roof is original TPO from 2015 (~11 yrs, mid-life). Boiler replaced 2024 (mitigant).
- **OM page:** null
- **Why it matters:** A single-membrane roof and other major systems near end of service life are large, lumpy costs. Absent a PCA, they are unquantified and unreserved.
- **Estimated financial impact:** Roof replacement est. $1.5–2.5M within a typical hold — unreserved.
- **Recommended next action:** Commission a Property Condition Assessment; obtain roof age/warranty and a 12-year capital plan.
- **Additional DD required:** Yes

### R11 · DSCR / debt-service coverage  —  **MEDIUM** (L1)
- **Category:** Debt / Leverage
- **Evidence:** At 60.0% LTV / 6.3% / 30-yr, coverage is 1.41x during the 2-yr IO but only 1.19x once amortizing — below the 1.25x floor.
- **OM page:** null
- **Why it matters:** Coverage below 1.25x on a fully-amortizing basis means the asset barely services its debt once interest-only burns off — a refinancing and distribution risk.
- **Estimated financial impact:** Post-IO coverage cushion is thin; distributions compress when the loan begins amortizing.
- **Recommended next action:** Size debt to a 1.25x amortizing DSCR floor; stress the post-IO coverage before committing.
- **Additional DD required:** No

### R07 · Management-fee adequacy  —  **MEDIUM** (L1)
- **Category:** Expenses
- **Evidence:** Seller underwrites a 2.0% management fee vs a 3.0% market benchmark; T-12 shows $0 (self-managed) — no third-party benchmark.
- **OM page:** null
- **Why it matters:** A below-market management fee understates operating cost and overstates NOI. Mixed-use high-rises with ground-floor retail warrant 2.5–3.5%.
- **Estimated financial impact:** ~$96,590/yr understated → ≈$1,839,810 of value at 5.3%.
- **Recommended next action:** Underwrite management to 3.0% of EGI (market for a 12-story mixed-use asset).
- **Additional DD required:** No

### R17 · Property-tax & reassessment risk  —  **MEDIUM** (L1)
- **Category:** Tax
- **Evidence:** RE taxes $786,927 = 8.1% of EGI, grown only ~3%/yr off the assessor FMV; a sale near $124,638,000 FMV plus assessment-rate changes in Metro City create reassessment exposure not modeled.
- **OM page:** null
- **Why it matters:** A sale can trigger reassessment and assessment rates change; underwriting taxes flat to the current bill understates go-forward expense.
- **Estimated financial impact:** Each +10% to the tax bill ≈ $78,693/yr of NOI.
- **Recommended next action:** Model a reassessment-on-sale scenario at the purchase basis; confirm the current mill levy and assessment ratio.
- **Additional DD required:** Yes

### R04 · Renovation / rent-premium substantiation  —  **MEDIUM** (L1)
- **Category:** Value-Add
- **Evidence:** OM markets interior-upgrade premiums on a $/unit basis with no $/SF normalization and no achieved-lease evidence; the supporting ROI detail is referenced but not included.
- **OM page:** null
- **Why it matters:** Marketed upgrade premiums ($/unit/month) mean nothing without $/SF normalization and achieved-lease evidence — unit-size mix can masquerade as renovation lift (the classic OM overstatement).
- **Estimated financial impact:** Upgrade upside unverified — exclude from value until substantiated.
- **Recommended next action:** Obtain the 'ROIs & Amenities' data-room sheet; normalize premiums to $/SF against classic units of like size.
- **Additional DD required:** Yes

- **Category:** Comparables
- **Evidence:** Comp rent/PSF figures conflict between sections of the OM. Subject $2.94/SF vs the Central submarket average $3.28/SF.
- **OM page:** null

### R18 · Lease rollover & retail anchor risk  —  **MEDIUM** (L1)
- **Category:** Lease Rollover
- **Evidence:** Retail income volatility: anchor Anchor restaurant tenant (47.7% of retail SF) has a 2026 base-rent abatement; ~20.0% of retail SF rolls within the hold.

- **Why it matters:** Concentrated retail rollover and an anchor rent abatement create near-term income volatility that the blended pro forma masks.

### R16 · Regulatory exposure  —  **LOW** (L1)
- **Category:** Regulatory
- **Evidence:** Metro City: no statewide rent control (favorable), but the OM does not affirmatively disclose the absence of affordable/income-restricted units.
- **OM page:** null

## Insufficient data (must resolve before IC)
### R02 · Loss-to-lease disclosure  —  **INSUFFICIENT_DATA**
- **Category:** Revenue / Rent
- **Evidence:** No unit-level rent roll, no market-rent column and no stated loss-to-lease. Subject in-place $2,808 ($2.94/SF) vs a Central submarket average of $3.28/SF.
- **OM page:** null
- **Why it matters:** Loss-to-lease is the gap between in-place and market rent — the core of any rent upside thesis. Without a unit-level roll and market rents it cannot be verified.
- **Estimated financial impact:** Rent-upside thesis unquantifiable from the OM.
- **Recommended next action:** Obtain the full unit-level rent roll with market-rent column; compute LTL by unit and by floor plan.
- **Additional DD required:** Yes

### R10 · Cap-rate & pricing sufficiency  —  **INSUFFICIENT_DATA** · guardrail
- **Category:** Pricing / Valuation
- **Evidence:** OM is unpriced and free-and-clear — no asking price or going-in cap. At the assessor FMV ($124,638,000): 5.3% on re-underwritten NOI vs 5.5% on the seller's Year-1 NOI.
- **OM page:** null
- **Why it matters:** An OM offered unpriced gives no going-in cap or price-per-unit anchor. Value must be triangulated from re-underwritten NOI and a cap-rate matrix, not the seller's numbers.
- **Estimated financial impact:** Each 25 bps of cap ≈ $6,296,573 of value swing at this NOI.
- **Recommended next action:** Confirm pricing guidance; value off re-underwritten NOI via a cap-rate sensitivity matrix; do not bid to the seller's Year-1 NOI.
- **Additional DD required:** Yes

### R12 · Leverage / LTV  —  **PASS**
- **Category:** Debt / Leverage
- **Evidence:** Assumed LTV 60.0% is conservative (≤75.0%).
- **OM page:** null
- **Why it matters:** Leverage above 75% leaves a thin equity cushion against value declines.
- **Estimated financial impact:** None — mitigant present.
- **Recommended next action:** Keep leverage ≤65–70% given the aggressive OM basis.
- **Additional DD required:** No

### R13 · Debt yield  —  **PASS**
- **Category:** Debt / Leverage
- **Evidence:** Debt yield 8.8% on re-underwritten NOI — above the 8.0% floor.
- **OM page:** null
- **Why it matters:** Debt yield (NOI ÷ loan) is the lender's downside test; below ~8% signals aggressive proceeds relative to income.
- **Estimated financial impact:** None — mitigant present.
- **Recommended next action:** Confirm lender debt-yield floor; size proceeds to ≥8% on re-underwritten NOI.
- **Additional DD required:** No

### R14 · Submarket supply / demand fundamentals  —  **PASS**
- **Category:** Market
- **Evidence:** Central submarket shows constrained supply: office vacancy 4.0%, retail 2.0%, est. MF vacancy ~2.0%; 1-mile avg HH income $210,151+; 1127 submarket units in the pipeline. No rent control disclosed.
- **OM page:** null
- **Why it matters:** Supply-constrained, high-income submarkets protect occupancy and pricing power — the demand side of the thesis. A PASS here proves the rule set discriminates rather than flagging everything.
- **Estimated financial impact:** None — mitigant present.
- **Recommended next action:** Confirm the multifamily (not office/retail) vacancy and 2024–2028 delivery pipeline with CoStar.
